claims.text: Ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides can be determined using ab initio VASP calculations.
GGA with the PBE functional is an appropriate approximation for determining ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
The proposed determination is performed at variable temperatures and magnetic fields.
Configurational entropy is a structural mediator relevant to ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
The average ionic radius of the A-site cation is a structural mediator relevant to ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
Electrical and magnetic properties of high-entropy oxides are correlated.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties is attributable to configurational entropy and the average A-site ionic radius.
Configurational entropy and average A-site ionic radius influence the intensity of indirect super-exchange interactions.
Configurational entropy and average A-site ionic radius influence the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters.
VASP calculations using GGA-PBE can predict the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
The baseline is the absence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
High-entropy oxides with varying configurational entropy and average A-site ionic radius can be compared computationally.
Magnetic moment, configurational entropy, and average A-site ionic radius are the proposed measured variables.
A lack of consistency between calculated and experimental ferromagnetic ground-state results would falsify the hypothesis.
